subject: physics
title: Light Dimmer
summary: Squeeze light through a gap so a dark band hits the target, then dim a lamp with one polaroid and then with three.
learningOutcome: The student can use a sin θ = nλ for the dark bands of a single slit, use Malus’ law I = I₀cos²θ, and find the light through a third polaroid between crossed ones.

levels.title: Flap’s gap
levels.adds: Baseline: the n-th dark band of a single slit is at a sin θ = nλ, so a wider gap makes a narrower pattern (Section 10.6).
hints: The dark bands are where the light from the two halves of the gap cancels: a sin θ = nλ.
So a = nλ / sin θ. Keep a and λ in the same unit.
A test shot tells you where the dark band falls for the width you have set.

levels.title: Glare’s shade
levels.adds: New idea: a polaroid halves unpolarised light and the next passes cos²θ of what is left (Malus’ law, Section 10.7).
hints: Unpolarised light loses half at the first polaroid.
The second passes cos²θ of what remains, so the fraction is ½cos²θ.
Solve ½cos²θ = the wanted fraction for θ.

levels.title: The middle polaroid
levels.adds: Apply it: a polaroid at θ between crossed ones passes I₀cos²θ sin²θ = (I₀/4) sin²2θ, the most at 45° (Example 10.2).
hints: After the first polaroid the light is I₀. The middle one passes I₀cos²θ.
The last is 90° from the first, so it makes an angle (90° − θ) with the middle one: cos²(90° − θ) = sin²θ.
I = (I₀/4) sin²2θ. The same value is reached at θ and at 90° − θ.

misconceptions: A narrower slit makes a narrower diffraction pattern
A polaroid between crossed polaroids cannot let any light through
A second polaroid at 45° halves the light that reaches it
